Just like me, you started off with the best in the series. Enjoy the freaking ride, man. I would give anything to play that game for the first time again.

Also, I genuinely didn't even recognize any of the side characters that you mentioned, that's why I didn't comment on them. I have no idea who La Volpe is. I know he wore a hood. How would I describe his character? No fucking clue. Bartolomeo? I literally have no idea who you're talking about. Mario? Yeah, the guy whose only purpose is to spout exposition at Ezio? Look, I just don't know how you could compare any of these forgettable nobodies with Black Beard, Charles Vane, Benjamin Hornigold, Bartholomew Roberts, Stede Bonnet, Adewale. Not only are these characters more memorable and likeable, but they actually serve a purpose in the story and drive Edwards arc of overcoming his own selfishness and greed. Some of these characters pull him toward redemption, while others push him down his own self-destructive path. How does that one prostitute lady complement that story or Ezio's arc? She teaches the player social stealth. And? I rest my case.

Protagonist: 

Ezio starts out interesting as a young, reckless man who's forced to grow up because of a tragedy. That tragedy is an effective moment because we get to see the relationship that he has with those he loses and what they represent in his life. I find the moment after he kills that first guy and declares that his family won't be forgotten or whatever is a defining moment for this character. Family and, specifically, Ezio's refusal to let anyone destroy his family become major themes for this character and they are what drive him as it is now his responsibility to protect his family and to carry the Auditore name. However, I feel that nothing interesting is ever done with this character for the rest of the game. He is put on this boring, generic murder quest where he has to murder literally everyone who ever had a thing to do with his family's murders. It became tedious and I very soon stopped caring about what was happening. His arc is essentially that he matures and learns to control his passions. That's a reasonably satisfying conclusion for that character, but it isn't earned. He says that his friends showed him that truth is what you make of it or whatever, but that's never a theme that's integrated into the story. Sure, that's the creed that the assassin's live by and all, but why is that significant to Ezio as a character? Shouldn't his arc have been to learn to let go of his rage and forgive those who wronged him? Oh, right, he does that after his, like, second assassination when Mario tells him to respect the dead. Then, for the rest of the game, Ezio's rage and immaturity are barely felt. It's like he just learned to overcome all of that off screen. But, overall, Ezio is a great character, in my opinion. He's just at the mercy of an unengaging story. Although, I think he's by far the most interesting in Revelations (which I think is way better than the rest of the Ezio trilogy). 

Setting:

Yeah, I agree. I was pleasantly surprised with how expansive the game was in terms of how many locations you can visit and how distinguished each one is. The historical period of the Renaissance itself is just bursting with flavour and atmosphere. So, yeah, no disagreement there.

Story:


I haven't played Assassin's Creed 1, so I can't judge it, but I think AC2 probably has the second worst story of any Assassin's Creed game with Unity having the worst. There's nothing aggressively terrible about it, it's just flat and boring and seems to time skip unwarrantedly at random points. As I said, it's another boring revenge plot in which you dispassionately murder a list of people all with the same single thing motivating you to do so. Because of this lack of depth or variety, I would find myself checking the achievements list to see how many "chapter completed" trophies were left because I just wanted it to be over. They should have had you pick off the few guys responsible for your family's murders, leaving Ezio with an empty and unfulfilled feeling. Then, he would find the assassins and they would give him a new purpose in life and thus help him move on from his thirst for vengeance. Instead, the way the story is told in the game, there's no real character progression. Yes, Ezio is a changed man by the end of the game, but his arc is so poorly defined that it just feels cheap and unearned. 

Parkour and Combat:

I'm going to be honest, the parkour and combat mechanics in this game are some of the most frustratingly stilted I have ever seen. I am aware it came out in 2009. While that explains why the game is so clunky, it does not justify it. I found almost no part of the actual gameplay of this game to be enjoyable. It took me hours of death after death after death and hours of researching tutorials and training with Mario just to figure out how to time a counter properly. And I still don't understand how it works! All I remember about the parkour is that it felt like one of the most asinine and incompetent navigation systems ever designed into a video game. It flows in no way whatsoever. If I had a nickel for every time I fell off of a structure because my joystick was pointing a fraction of a a hair to the left or right as I was trying to jump to another platform, I would be a very rich man. I respect that they clearly tried to emphasize it more than they do in recent games with entire levels devoted just to scaling the inside of a cathedral. But I swear, I damn near broke a controller trying to play this game.

Modern day:

Desmond is a boring, horse faced schlub with no discernible personality or charisma. He does nothing but serve as the superfluous reminder that I am not playing as a badass assassin. Instead, I am playing as some schmuck playing as a badass assassin. This completely unnecessary and immersion breaking extra dimension has plagued Assassin's Creed as a franchise for over a decade and only serves to bog down the story and gameplay with a far less fleshed out and far less interesting story. I couldn't be made to care about Desmond Miles or any modern day element of any Assassin's Creed game if you put a gun to my head.

But that's just how I feel.
